attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts and endorses the proposition.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the universal historical assertion and firm, unlimited-horizon forecast.

contract.note: Sustained service-level viability without individual token billing is a fair reading. The operational definition of economic feasibility matters.

evidence.note: A dated report of Gamma's CEO claiming company profitability. It does not establish matched billing terms and sustained service-level economics, and is not an independent profitability finding.

reviews.rationale: Gamma's reported profitability is relevant potential counterevidence but does not meet the documented-counterexample requirements. The packet establishes neither the historical impossibility nor a constraint covering all future services.

attribution.note: This is Zitron's own endorsed prediction.

semantics.note: Calling the transition inevitable is a firm commitment despite the introductory 'I think'. The majority threshold and absence of a deadline are preserved.

contract.note: Counting subscription products is a reasonable ordinary reading, though not uniquely specified. The missing representative denominator prevents resolution under the plausible alternatives.

evidence.note: GitHub discloses an implemented credit-based billing transition. This single product family cannot establish a market-wide majority, and the excerpt does not explain the credits' token linkage.
The dated preprint concerns selected offerings with substantial missing pricing. Usage quotas are broader than token billing, and the study does not establish a majority transition.

reviews.rationale: Neither item establishes that more than half of a representative subscription population changed to token-based billing. No deadline or qualifying conclusive event permits a final score.

attribution.note: Zitron directly makes the conditional prediction.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves eventual investor scrutiny and the antecedent that revenue growth fails to keep pace with rising R&D spending involving token costs.

contract.note: An analyst's earnings-call question reasonably constitutes investor scrutiny. Reading the revenue condition as growth lagging relevant spending is ordinary; neither a widespread revolt nor negative revenue growth was required.

evidence.note: SAP's disclosed revenue growth establishes part of the antecedent when matched with e2's R&D comparison. This excerpt does not itself demonstrate investor scrutiny.
The July 23 analyst question scrutinizes 14% R&D cost growth and its token component. Management attributes part of the increase to tokens; the same call reports 11% revenue growth.

reviews.rationale: The post-publication SAP call meets the early-resolution rule: an investment analyst questioned rising R&D costs involving tokens while R&D growth exceeded revenue growth. Management's productivity defense does not negate the observed scrutiny.

attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts both the losses and the revenue requirement.

semantics.note: The normalization fairly captures the current financial assessment and the claimed revenue gap against ongoing Oracle obligations. It does not predict a dated payment default.

contract.note: The latest completed annual period is a reasonable baseline for this annual comparison. The contract appropriately distinguishes future completed-capacity obligations from bills already payable; baseline and payment scope remain interpretive choices.

evidence.note: The reporting supports substantial 2025 losses and describes separate FT document review. It distinguishes operating losses, headline net loss and a major noncash charge; it is secondary reporting rather than direct access to audited accounts.
Provides the comparable realized annual revenue baseline. Cash burn is not net income, and this report supplies no Oracle-specific payment schedule.
Reports a future purchase commitment beginning in 2027. It does not establish annual payment amounts or bills payable during the observation period.
Materially qualifies the headline loss through an adjusted measure excluding noncash items. That different accounting basis cannot replace unadjusted net income or establish Oracle payment coverage.

reviews.rationale: Substantial losses are supported, including after considering the noncash-charge qualification. The packet does not establish the relevant recurring Oracle payment schedule or independently verify the completed-capacity estimate. The combined proposition remains unsettled.
